stories.title: Find where a beam ray meets the skin
stories.description: Create src/needle/entry.ts with skinEntry(volume, ray): the ray comes from src/core/geometry.ts unproject (origin = the X-ray source, which is under the table, in front of the prone patient; direction = source → detector). The needle goes in from the BACK, which faces the detector, so do not walk from the source (that finds the belly skin). Instead start where the ray leaves the volume's grid on the detector side and walk back toward the source, in steps of at most half the smallest voxel spacing, and return the first point whose label (labelAt in src/needle/sample.ts) is not air — the skin entry point on the detector side — or null if the ray never meets tissue inside the grid. Refine the hit to within 0.1 mm by halving the last step. Plain TypeScript, no browser code; no edits in src/core/.
acceptance: Unit test (phantom, pose 0°/0°): the ray through the image centre gives a point on the BACK: y > 30 mm (the phantom's back skin is near y = 42), whose label is not air while the point 1 voxel further toward the detector is air (the skin boundary, within 1 voxel)
Unit test (phantom, pose 0°/0°): the returned point is not on the belly side (y < −30 never happens for 5 pixels inside the body)

Unit test (phantom): for 5 pixels inside the body and for 2 oblique poses, the returned point projects with geometry.project to the pixel the ray was made from, within 0.5 px, and every sample from it toward the detector up to the grid's edge is air (it is the detector-side skin)
Unit test: a ray that misses the body (an image corner at pose 0°/0°) returns null
Unit test: a volume not in the standard layout is rejected
stories.notes: Review fix 2026-11-13 (owner approved all review fixes): walk from the detector side, so the entry is on the back (the first draft walked from the source and would have found the belly skin).

stories.title: Keep one needle session that obeys the handling rules
stories.description: Create src/needle/session.ts: a plain-TypeScript needle session that wraps the F4 model (src/needle/model.ts). It holds the chosen needle id and pre-bend (0–30° in steps of 5°), the entry point and the model (null before an entry is marked). Functions: chooseNeedle(id), choosePreBend(deg), markEntry(point, beamDirection) (beamDirection = the ray's source → detector direction; creates the model with insertion direction = MINUS beamDirection, so the needle goes from the back into the body toward the source and is seen end-on, 'down the beam', F5.3), setHubAngles (each axis clamped to ±45° of the start, F5.4), nudgeHub(dPitch, dYaw), advance(mm), withdraw(mm), rotateBevel(deg), withdrawFully() (removes the needle). While the inserted depth is above 0, chooseNeedle, choosePreBend and markEntry change nothing and report 'locked' (F5.1); after withdrawFully they work again. For the curved-tip RF cannula the pre-bend is its built-in curve (owner decision 2026-11-11), so choosePreBend has no effect for it. toNeedleState() gives the shared NeedleState. No browser code, no edits in src/core/. Also correct the comment on CreateNeedleInput.direction in src/needle/model.ts (it says 'F5 passes the beam direction'; it should say F5 passes the reversed beam direction, detector → source). Comment only, no code change in model.ts.
acceptance: Unit test: before insertion, choosing a needle and a pre-bend changes them; a pre-bend that is not a multiple of 5 or is outside 0–30 is rejected
Unit test: after markEntry and advance(1), chooseNeedle, choosePreBend and markEntry are refused (locked) and the needle stays the same; after withdrawFully they are accepted again

Unit test (F5.3): right after markEntry, the needle's direction (entry point minus hub) is OPPOSITE to the beam direction passed in (angle 180° within 0.1°); at pose 0°/0° advancing 5 mm moves the tip toward −y (into the body from the back)
Unit test (F5.4): setHubAngles(60, -70) is clamped to (45, -45); nudgeHub never goes past ±45°
Unit test: the same sequence of calls always gives an identical NeedleState (deterministic)
stories.notes: Review fix 2026-11-13 (owner approved all review fixes): the needle points against the beam direction (detector → source), matching the F4 model's tests, which insert toward the front (−y).

stories.title: Show the needle and pre-bend pickers and publish the needle to the store
stories.description: In src/needle/index.ts build the needle panel's set-up row: a needle picker (data-testid needle-select, one entry per catalogue needle, by name) and a pre-bend picker (data-testid prebend-select, 0–30° in 5° steps; disabled for the curved-tip cannula). Keep one session (F5-S2) for the app, exported as needleSession from src/needle/session.ts, and write its NeedleState to store.needle whenever it changes (null when there is no needle). On caseStart, and when store.volume changes to a different volume, the needle is removed (default from F5–F7 planning; see notes). Register a debug getter 'needle' returning { needleId, preBend, locked, entryPoint, hubAngles, bevelAngle, insertedDepth, tip } or null. Pickers are disabled while locked. Every new control is at least 44×44 px in the tablet set-up. Marking an entry from an image pixel is the next story (F5-S12).
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups): the needle picker lists all six catalogue needles; picking one (select on desktop, tap + choose on tablet) changes window.__sim.needle().needleId
Screen test (both set-ups): the pre-bend picker offers 0, 5, … 30; picking 15 shows 15 in the getter; for the curved-tip cannula the pre-bend picker is disabled
Screen test (tablet): both pickers are at least 44×44 px
Unit test: emitting caseStart on a test store/bus removes the needle (store.needle becomes null)
Unit test: putting a different volume into a test store removes the needle; putting the same volume back does not
stories.verify: npx playwright test tests/e2e/needle/pickers.spec.ts && npx vitest run tests/needle/storeLink.test.ts
stories.notes: Owner decision 2026-11-13 (accepted every F5–F7 planning default): the needle is removed on caseStart and when a different volume is loaded. Review fix 2026-11-13 (owner approved all review fixes): split in two (marking from a pixel moved to F5-S12); a test for removal on a new volume added.

stories.title: Mark the entry from an image pixel, with a screen-test helper
stories.description: Add markEntryAtPixel(pixel) to the app's needle session (src/needle/session.ts): it marks the entry where the ray through that image pixel, at store.lastImagePose, meets the skin on the detector side (F5-S1), with the needle pointing against that ray's direction (F5-S2, F5.3); it does nothing before the first image or while locked. Write the zone's screen-test helper tests/e2e/needle/needlePage.ts that calls needleSession.markEntryAtPixel through the dev server's module (the same trick as setPose; zone helpers are not shared).
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups, phantom, after one image at 0°/0°): markEntryAtPixel((256, 256)) through the helper gives an entry point on the back (y > 30), not air, with air 1 voxel further toward the detector, projecting to (256, 256) within 2 px; the same at oblique 20° and pixel (240, 270) (F5.2 logic)
Screen test (both set-ups): right after marking, the needle points against the beam (window.__sim.needle() tip is the entry point and advancing 5 mm moves the tip toward the source)
Screen test (both set-ups): before the first image markEntryAtPixel does nothing
stories.notes: Review fix 2026-11-13 (owner approved all review fixes): split out of F5-S3.

stories.title: Mark the skin entry point from a tap on the fluoro image
stories.description: Add a Mark entry tool button (data-testid mark-entry) to the needle panel. While it is active and no needle is inserted, an 'imageTap' bus event (payload ImageTap: the pixel of the held image as taken, src/core/store.ts) calls markEntryAtPixel (F5-S3) with that pixel. The tool then switches off. The tool is disabled before the first image and while the needle is inserted. The render zone emits 'imageTap' from the canvas (F7-S7); this story's screen tests emit the bus event themselves through the dev server's store module (the setPose trick). Every new control is at least 44×44 px in the tablet set-up. This is the feature's last loop story: run the whole check.
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups, phantom, after one image at pose 0°/0°): with Mark entry on, emitting imageTap at pixel (256, 256) gives the same entry point as markEntryAtPixel((256, 256)), and the tool switches off
Screen test (both set-ups): with Mark entry off, imageTap changes nothing
Screen test (both set-ups): Mark entry is disabled before the first image
Screen test (both set-ups): after marking an entry and advancing 1 mm, Mark entry is disabled and imageTap changes nothing; after Withdraw fully it is enabled again
Screen test (tablet): the Mark entry button is at least 44×44 px
stories.verify: npx playwright test tests/e2e/needle/markEntry.spec.ts && npm run check
stories.notes: Owner decision 2026-11-13 (accepted every F5–F7 planning default): the bus event `imageTap` (payload ImageTap { x, y } from src/core/store.ts) is on the shared contract. Unblocked. Review fix 2026-11-13 (owner approved all review fixes): test for 'disabled while inserted' added; depends on F5-S12 and F5-S13.

stories.title: Steer the needle with the keyboard
stories.description: Desktop keys (F5.4): W / S advance / withdraw 1 mm per press (0.2 mm with Shift), Q / E rotate the bevel −15° / +15°, arrow keys change the hub angle by 1° (Up/Down = pitch toward 12 / 6 o'clock, Right/Left = yaw toward 3 / 9 o'clock). Keys act only when a needle exists, the disclaimer is not shown (data-disclaimer), the screen is the simulator (data-screen 'sim' when the attribute is set), and focus is not in a text field, slider or picker. Register the keys as group 'Needle' in src/core/shortcuts.ts's shared list (registering is allowed; the file itself is not edited) so the help overlay lists them.
acceptance: Screen test (desktop, after marking an entry): W advances insertedDepth by 1 mm, Shift+W by 0.2 mm, S withdraws 1 mm
Screen test (desktop): Q and E change bevelAngle by −15° and +15° (kept within 0–360)
Screen test (desktop): each arrow key changes the matching hub angle by 1°
Screen test (desktop): with focus on a C-arm slider, an arrow key does not change the needle
Screen test (desktop): pressing ? shows a 'Needle' group in the help overlay listing W / S, Q / E and the arrow keys
Keys are a desktop-only behaviour: these tests skip the tablet set-up; the tablet equivalents are tested in F5-S7 and F5-S8

stories.title: Steer the needle with the mouse on the control pad
stories.description: Add a needle control pad (data-testid needle-pad) to the needle panel. On desktop, dragging on it changes the hub angles (right = yaw toward 3 o'clock, up = pitch toward 12 o'clock; 0.2° per pixel, draft value), clamped to ±45° from the start. The scroll wheel over the pad advances (wheel up) or withdraws (wheel down) 1 mm per wheel step, or 0.2 mm with Shift; the wheel over the pad does not scroll the page. The pad is at least 44×44 px in the tablet set-up.
acceptance: Screen test (desktop): dragging 50 px right on the pad raises hubAngles.yaw by 10° (±1°); dragging 50 px up raises pitch by 10° (±1°)
Screen test (desktop): a long drag stops at 45°
Screen test (desktop): one wheel step up advances 1 mm, with Shift 0.2 mm; one step down withdraws 1 mm
Screen test (desktop): the page does not scroll when the wheel is used over the pad
stories.notes: Owner decision 2026-11-13 (accepted every F5–F7 planning default): drag 0.2° per pixel; the wheel steers only over the needle pad (accepted as drafts the owner may tune later).

stories.title: Steer and twist the needle with touch on the control pad
stories.description: Tablet controls on the needle pad (F5.5): a one-finger drag changes the hub angles exactly as the mouse drag does; a two-finger twist rotates the bevel by the twist angle (clockwise twist = clockwise on the clock face). Add zone touch helpers in tests/e2e/needle/touch.ts (CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent, like tests/e2e/view3d/touch.ts; zone helpers are not shared).
acceptance: Screen test (tablet): a 50 px one-finger drag to the right raises hubAngles.yaw by 10° (±1°)
Screen test (tablet): a 45° clockwise two-finger twist on the pad changes bevelAngle by +45° (±5°); counter-clockwise by −45°
Screen test (tablet): touching the pad does not scroll the page

stories.title: Add Advance and Withdraw buttons that step or move while held
stories.description: Add Advance (data-testid needle-advance) and Withdraw (data-testid needle-withdraw) buttons to the needle panel. A tap or click moves 1 mm. Held for longer than 300 ms, the needle keeps moving at 5 mm per second until release (draft numbers). Each button is at least 44×44 px in the tablet set-up.
acceptance: Screen test (both set-ups; click on desktop, tap on tablet): one press of Advance adds 1 mm to insertedDepth, one press of Withdraw takes 1 mm away
Screen test (both set-ups): holding Advance for 1 s adds between 4 and 7 mm, and the depth stops changing after release
Screen test (tablet): both buttons are at least 44×44 px
stories.notes: Owner decision 2026-11-13 (accepted every F5–F7 planning default): hold delay 300 ms and 5 mm/s (accepted as drafts).

stories.title: Show depth, bevel clock face and angle to the beam
stories.description: Add readouts to the needle panel (F5.6): inserted depth in mm with one decimal (data-testid needle-depth), a clock-face bevel indicator (data-testid needle-bevel, with data-angle = bevelAngle and the notch drawn at that clock position, 12 o'clock = head, as on a real hub), and the angle between the needle's outside part (hub → entry point) and the beam ray from the current C-arm pose's source through the entry point, in whole degrees (data-testid needle-beam-angle). The angle is between the two LINES, 0–90°, whichever way each points (the needle points against the beam, so a naive vector angle would read 180°). Put the angle maths in a plain function (src/needle/readouts.ts) with a unit test. Withdraw fully and the lock checks are the next story (F5-S13).
acceptance: Unit test: a needle pointing exactly against the beam gives 0°, and so does one pointing along it; tilted 30° away gives 30° (±0.5°); the result is never above 90°
Screen test (both set-ups): after advancing 12.4 mm the depth readout shows 12.4
Screen test (both set-ups): after rotating the bevel to 90°, needle-bevel has data-angle 90
Screen test (both set-ups): right after marking an entry the beam angle shows 0; after changing the hub by 10° it shows 10 (±1)
stories.verify: npx vitest run tests/needle/readouts.test.ts && npx playwright test tests/e2e/needle/readouts.spec.ts
stories.notes: Owner decision 2026-11-13 (accepted every F5–F7 planning default): the beam angle is measured against the CURRENT C-arm pose's beam. Review fix 2026-11-13 (owner approved all review fixes): angle is between lines (0–90°); Withdraw fully and lock tests moved to F5-S13.
